archetype: Cooldown-driven bossing thief that steals and re-uses Explorer skills. hexa.orderMethodology: The class doc publishes a 93-row table titled 'Skill Upgrade Order', dated 09-29-2025 in its own heading and credited to aCyr for compiling it. It is modelled against Hard Limbo phase 1. It has TWO separate columns because the binding resource differs by server type: 'fd % per fragment (heroic)' and 'fd % per energy (interactive)'. The Heroic column is the one a GMS Heroic planner should use. Both columns are sorted strictly descending by efficiency, so the row order IS the recommended purchase order.

interactiveOrderDiffers.claim: The Interactive (Sol Erda energy) order diverges from the Heroic (fragment) order from the fifth purchase onward. interactiveOrderDiffers.why: Heroic and Interactive are gated by different currencies, so the cost denominator differs and the optimal order differs with it. A Heroic planner must not present the Interactive column.

gearingNotes:
Phantom's gearing is unusual in three ways, all of them well sourced.

1. CRITICAL RATE IS SELF-SUPPLIED AND CAPS EARLY. The class doc publishes a full accounting of how a GMS Phantom reaches exactly 100% crit: 5% base, 35% from the Piercing Vision passive, 20% from its own Phantom Link at Lv.3, 10% from Lynn Link Lv.3, 10% from Decent Sharp Eyes, 4% from the Night Lord Lv.200 legion member bonus, 4% from the Marksman Lv.200 legion member bonus, 1% from an Ocean or Holy badge, and 11% from Hyper Stats at level 8. The wiki independently confirms the two largest in-class contributors - Piercing Vision at max gives Critical Rate +35% and Final Damage +30%, and Phantom Instinct at Lv.3 gives Critical Rate +20% plus Damage +5%. The practical consequence is the doc's own advice: push crit onto the Legion Grid and Legion Artifact so you can DROP hyper stat crit levels and spend those points elsewhere. Any generic 'max crit rate hyper stat' advice is actively wrong for this class.

2. COOLDOWN REDUCTION IS A DAMAGE STAT, AND A CD HAT IS THE RECOMMENDED HAT. The class doc recommends a cooldown-reduction hat paired with the Lv.200 Mercedes legion member bonus, and publishes a conversion table of cooldown to equivalent final damage (estimated, by the doc's own note, via Maple Scouter): -5s CD is about 6.0% FD; -4s CD plus one line of LUK% is also about 6.0% FD; -4s CD alone about 5.1% FD; -3s CD plus one line LUK% about 4.8% FD; -2s CD plus two lines LUK% about 4.2% FD; -3s CD alone about 3.9% FD; -2s CD plus one line LUK% about 3.4% FD; three lines of LUK% about 2.8% FD; -2s CD alone about 2.5% FD. The doc also tabulates the resulting cooldowns with a Lv.250 Mercedes: Tempest with the Cooldown Cutter hyper passive falls from 13.536s at base to 9.268s at -5s CD; Ace in the Hole from 14.1s to 9.55s; Rift Break, Phantom's Mark and Rose Finale from 28.2s to 23.2s. Without the Mercedes bonus, Tempest's base cooldown is 18s (14.4s with the hyper).

3. IGNORE DEFENSE IS UNUSUALLY HIGH FROM THE KIT. The class doc puts Phantom's innate combined IED at about 44.8%, from Priere D'Aria's passive 30% (+1% with Decent Combat Orders) plus Tempest's 20% one-minute debuff; Grandis' own skill-derived table independently lists Ignore DEF +44%, and the wiki confirms the two components (Priere D'Aria Lv.30: Damage +45%, Ignore Defense 30%; Tempest Lv.30: Enemy DEF Ignored 20% for 60s). A Phantom therefore needs less IED from gear and potential than a class starting from zero.

OTHER GEARING FACTS. Attack speed from the class's own passives is 7 (Grandis), and the class doc considers attack speed largely wasted on Phantom for bossing. Phantom has no Final Attack skill, which the class doc calls out explicitly because it means the Legion Artifact 'Final Attack Skill Damage %' line is worth nothing to this class. Tempest's attacks are always critical hits (wiki), which is part of why crit rate saturates so easily. The class's legion effect is %Mesos Obtained rather than a damage stat. Recommended familiar badges per the class doc: Ocean (+1% Damage, +1% Crit Rate, easily obtained), Apocalypse, Lion, Holy, Labyrinth and Showa.

STOLEN SKILLS ARE A REAL PROGRESSION AXIS. Phantom equips stolen Explorer skills into Impeccable Memory slots I through IV plus a Hyper tier, managed with Skill Swipe and Loadout. The wiki records the hard mechanical constraints: passive effects of stolen skills do not work, a skill may only go into a slot of equal or higher rank, a skill cannot be used immediately after being assigned, Bishop's Heal has its cooldown increased when stolen, and the stolen skill's level is capped by the Impeccable Memory slot's level. The class doc's boost-node captions add that Impeccable Memory boost nodes raise stolen-skill DAMAGE only and do nothing for stolen buff effects. Final Cut (a stolen skill) is the buff the doc's buff-duration advice is built around. A planner that models Phantom without a stolen-skill loadout slot is missing a system unique to the class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading the class doc's Legion Artifact priority list as if it were the HEXA Stat priority.
commonMistakes.detail: The doc lists Legion Artifact stats as Damage, Boss Damage, Crit Damage, All Stat, ATT/MATT, Cooldown Skip, Item Drop Rate, EXP, IED, Critical Chance, Buff Duration, Meso. Its HEXA Stat guidance is a different and shorter list: ATT, then Critical Damage, then LUK. These are two different systems in two different sections and have been conflated in at least one secondary summary of this doc.

commonMistakes.mistake: Maxing the Critical Rate hyper stat.
commonMistakes.detail: Phantom reaches 100% crit with the Critical Rate hyper stat at only level 8. The class doc's advice runs the other way - reduce that hyper stat level by taking crit from the Legion Grid and Legion Artifact instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a boost node trio list published before v.269.
commonMistakes.detail: Grandis Library's Phantom page carries a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which is direct evidence Phantom's boost node groupings changed at that patch. mastermysty's widely-linked cross-class trio table is dated 2024-11-21 and therefore describes the old groupings.

commonMistakes.mistake: Placing the ATT HEXA Stat on the highest-level slot by reflex.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc specifically warns that the slot giving the most ATT is not necessarily the highest-level slot, and says to place ATT by actual ATT yield first, then Critical Damage on the next-highest level, then LUK.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying the Interactive HEXA order on a Heroic character.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc's upgrade table is split into a fragment-limited Heroic column and an energy-limited Interactive column, and they diverge from the fifth purchase. Defying Fate levels 2-4 sit seventh on Interactive but twenty-second on Heroic.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling attack speed on Inner Ability.
commonMistakes.detail: Phantom is already at attack speed 7 from its own passives, and the class doc says attack speed only helps windup and cast animations, making it generally unnecessary for bossing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Chasing buff duration past Final Cut's 100% uptime expecting more damage.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc's own threshold note is that beyond full Final Cut uptime, extra buff duration buys you a held iframe, not extra damage.

consensusAssessment:
Three sources independent of one another were reached - the class doc, mastermysty's node table, and maplestorywiki. But they are not three independent JUDGEMENT sources, and the file should be presented accordingly.

MECHANICAL FACTS (skill names, crit and IED contributions, cooldowns, attack speed, link and legion effects) are strong: independently confirmed across the class doc, the wiki and Grandis' API-derived stat table.

JUDGEMENT (HEXA investment order, 5th-job node priority, inner ability, hyper skill passives, HEXA stat placement) rests on ONE current source, the Phantom class doc. Grandis Library restates that same doc by its own admission and is not a second vote. mastermysty is genuinely independent but covers boost node trios only and is dated 2024-11-21, before the v.269 regrouping, so it cannot corroborate anything current.

The HEXA order in particular - the most valuable content in this file - is single-source. It is unusually well-founded for a single source (an explicit efficiency model, a stated boss benchmark, a named compiler, its own date, and a Heroic/Interactive split), but a planner should surface it as one class-community model rather than as settled consensus.

No hyper stat priority exists for Phantom in any reachable source, and that field is correctly empty.

conflicts.positionA: The generic cross-class advice circulating on aggregator sites is to activate mastery nodes, then boost nodes, then HEXA stat, with the origin skill treated as an early cornerstone.
conflicts.positionB: The Phantom class doc's Heroic efficiency model places Defying Fate level 2 twenty-second in the purchase order, behind four mastery unlocks, many mastery levels and three of the four enhancement nodes.
conflicts.status: Recorded, not resolved. Only the class doc's position is sourced to a Phantom-specific model; the generic position was not verified from any source that analysed Phantom. A planner should show the class doc's order and should not blend it with generic advice.

gaps: No hyper stat priority order exists for Phantom in any reachable source. The class doc has no hyper stat section; Grandis publishes none for any class. Field left null deliberately.

The class doc's 'Stolen Skill Library' section is effectively empty as text - it consists of images and carries its own note that Pathfinder is missing. No recommended stolen-skill loadout for training or bossing could be extracted, despite this being Phantom's most class-unique decision. This needs a vision pass over the doc or a read of the Phantom Discord.

Grandis Library's Phantom 6th-job infographics (Main / Legion Champion, and Mule) are images and were not read. For other classes these carry per-play-pattern HEXA investment order, so they may contain a second view of the HEXA order specific to boss-mule Phantoms.
The class doc contains no mention of Sol Janus, Sol Hecate or Ascent, so it offers no guidance on HEXA skill cores beyond the origin/mastery/enhancement set. Left empty rather than inferred.
The V-matrix example matrices and the 'Ideal Hexa Matrix Setup Example' are images; exact target node levels were not extractable.

defects: THE BOOST NODE TIERING IS MISATTRIBUTED TO GRANDIS. I re-fetched grandislibrary.com/heroes/phantom and read the tier labels directly. Grandis says: Node 1 PRIMARY, Node 2 PRIMARY, Node 3 SECONDARY, Node 4 SECONDARY, Node 5 OTHER, Node 6 OTHER. The file puts Node 2 and Node 3 under 'secondary' and Nodes 4, 5 and 6 under 'other', and states the wrong tier inside each 'why' as a direct attribution — 'Node 2: ... Grandis' SECONDARY (frequently used) tier' and 'Node 4: Rose Carte Finale, Penombre — Grandis' OTHER tier'. This is a priority order no source states. It is actionable damage: it demotes Node 2 (Mille Aiguilles + Blason + Double Entendre, the main training node) out of build-first tier, and drops Rose Carte Finale to the bottom tier when the doc's own efficiency table makes Rose Finale VI 1 the single best HEXA purchase in the game for this class (0.1877%/fragment, rank 1 of 93).

Link skill numbers are unverified and partly contradicted. The file states 'Lv.1 Critical Rate +10%. Lv.3 Critical Rate +20% and Damage +5%', sourced only to maplestorywiki.net/w/Phantom/Skills. Grandis states 'Phantom Instinct' gives '+5% Damage and +15-20% Crit Rate' — i.e. no level in the range is +10%. The Lv.1 figure has no support in any source I could reach.
